==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈpi.pəl/|[ˈpʰi.pəɫ]|[ˈpʰi.pɫ̩]|a=GA}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-people.ogg|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈpiː.pəl/|[ˈpʰiː.pɫ̩]|a=RP}} ** {{audio|en|En-uk-people.ogg|a=UK}} * {{IPA|en|[ˈpi.pɯ̽ɫ]|a=Pacific Northwest,CA}} {{attn|en|check - is this right?}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈpipɨl/|/-ɐl/|a=Indic}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈpipol/|a=Philippines,and,NNSE}} * {{homophones|en|papal|peepul|pupil|a=some accents}} * {{hyphenation|en|peo|ple}} * {{rhymes|en|iːpəl|s=2}} ===Etymology 1=== {{ety|en|:inh|enm:peple}} From {{inh|en|enm|puple}}, {{m|enm|peple}}, {{m|enm|peeple}}, from {{derived|en|xno|people}}, from {{derived|en|fro|pueple}}, {{m|fro|peuple}}, {{m|fro|pople}}, from {{derived|en|la|populus|t=a people, nation}}, from {{der|en|itc-ola|populus}}, from earlier {{m|itc-ola|poplus}}, from even earlier {{m|itc-ola|poplos}}, from {{der|en|itc-pro|*poplos|t=army}} of unknown origin. {{doublet|en|pueblo}}. Gradually ousted native {{cog|en|lede}} and, partially, {{m|en|folk}}. Originally used with singular verbs (e.g. "the people is hungry, and weary, and thirsty, in the wilderness" in the King James Version of 2 Samuel 17:29{{R:King James Version|2 Samuel|17|29|page=426|column=2|text={{...}}The people ''is'' hungrie, and wearie, and thirſtie in the wilderneſſe.|nodot=1}}), the plural aspect of ''people'' is probably due to influence from {{cog|enm|lede}}, {{m|enm|leed}}, a plural since [[w:Old English|Old English]] times; see {{m|ang|lēode}}. ====Alternative forms==== * {{alter|en|peeps|peops||slang}} * {{alter|en|peple||obsolete}} * {{alter|en|pipple||pronunciation spelling}} * {{alter|en|ppl|ppl.||Internet slang|or|text messaging}} ====Noun==== {{en-noun|~}} # {{senseid|en|persons, plural of person}} {{plural of|en|person}}: a [[body]] of [[person]]s considered generally or collectively; a [[group]] of two or more [[person]]s. #: {{syn|en|peeps|q1=slang|lede|leod}} #: {{ux|en|There were so many '''people''' at the restaurant last night.}} #: {{ux|en|These six '''people''' are waiting for the bus.}} #: {{ux|en|Under dictatorship, '''people''' suffered and died.}} #* {{RQ:Austen Pride and Prejudice|passage="What a charming amusement for young '''people''' this is, Mr. Darcy! There is nothing like dancing after all. I consider it as one of the first refinements of polished society."|chapter=6}} #* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=12|passage=There were many wooden chairs for the bulk of his visitors, and two wicker armchairs with red cloth cushions for superior '''people'''. From the packing-cases had emerged some Indian clubs,{{nb...}}, and all these articles{{...}}made a scattered and untidy decoration that Mrs. Clough assiduously dusted and greatly cherished.}} #* {{RQ:Travers Cuckoo in the Nest|chapter=1|passage=“{{...}} the awfully hearty sort of Christmas cards that '''people''' do send to other '''people''' that they don't know at all well. You know. The kind that have mottoes like
  Here's rattling good luck and roaring good cheer, / With lashings of food and great hogsheads of beer.{{nb...}}”}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-01|volume=407|issue=8838|page=11|title=Towards the end of poverty|url=http://www.economist.com/news/leaders/21578665-nearly-1-billion-people-have-been-taken-out-extreme-poverty-20-years-world-should-aim|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/HjLZ6|archivedate=2024-09-05|passage=But poverty’s scourge is fiercest below $1.25 (the average of the 15 poorest countries’ own poverty lines, measured in 2005 dollars and adjusted for differences in purchasing power): '''people''' below that level live lives that are poor, nasty, brutish and short.|accessdate=3 June 2013}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=June 21 2013|author=w:Oliver Burkeman|volume=189|issue=2|page=27|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly |title=Conscious computing: how to take control of your life online |url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/technology/2013/may/10/conscious-computing-twitter-facebook-google |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130824175505/http://www.theguardian.com/technology/2013/may/10/conscious-computing-twitter-facebook-google|archivedate=August 24, 2013 |passage=The dirty secret of the internet is that all this distraction and interruption is immensely profitable. Web companies like to boast about{{nb...}}, or offering services that let you{{...}}"share the things you love with the world" and so on. But the real way to build a successful online business is to be better than your rivals at undermining '''people''''s control of their own attention.}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-29|volume=407|issue=8842|page=72–3|title=A punch in the gut|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/le1Hh|archivedate=2023-03-08|url=https://www.economist.com/science-and-technology/2013/06/29/a-punch-in-the-gut|passage=Mostly, the microbiome is beneficial. It helps with digestion and enables '''people''' to extract a lot more calories from their food than would otherwise be possible. Research over the past few years, however, has implicated it in diseases from atherosclerosis to asthma to autism.|accessdate=3 November 2018}} # {{senseid|en|group of persons, such as a nation}} {{lb|en|countable|collective}} {{U|person|s}} forming or belonging to a particular group, such as a [[nation]], [[class]], [[ethnic]] group, [[country]], [[family]], etc. #: {{syn|en|collective|community|congregation|folk}} #: {{cot|en|q1=sometimes synonymous|nation}} #: {{collocation|en|a '''people''' apart}} #: {{collocation|en|an industrious '''people'''}} #: {{collocation|en|the indigenous '''peoples''' of Europe}} #: {{collocation|en|the native '''peoples''' of Borneo}} #* {{RQ:Haggard She|passage=`So, oh Holly. This '''people''' was an old '''people''' before the Egyptians were.'}} #* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Hafsa Khalil|title=Electric blue tarantula species discovered in Thailand|url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/09/26/world/electric-blue-tarantula-discovered-thailand-scn-scli-intl|date=2023-09-26|passage=The team auctioned off the right to name the new species to publicize the find and raise awareness and funds for the indigenous Lahu '''people''' of northern Thailand, a group that Sippawat is part of.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20241120180012/https://www.cnn.com/2023/09/26/world/electric-blue-tarantula-discovered-thailand-scn-scli-intl/}} # {{senseid|en|group of persons subject to a ruler or leader}} A group of persons regarded as being [[servant]]s, [[follower]]s, [[companion]]s or [[subject]]s of a [[ruler]] or [[leader]]. #: {{collocation|en|Moses said, "Let my '''people''' go."}} #: {{collocation|en|his '''people''' were weary}} #: {{syn|en|fans|groupies|supporters}} #* {{RQ:KJV|2 Samuel|8|15|page=415|column=1|text=And Dauid reigned ouer all Iſrael, and Dauid executed iudgement and iuſtice vnto all his '''people'''.}} #* '''1952,''' ''{{w|Old Testament}}, {{w|Revised Standard Version}}'', Thomas Nelson & Sons, {{w|Book of Isaiah|Isaiah}} 1:3: # {{senseid|en|one's colleagues or employees}} One's [[colleague]]s or [[employee]]s. #: {{collocation|en|I'll have my '''people''' call your '''people'''.}} #: {{collocation|en|I have my '''people''' working on it.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2001|author=w:Vince Flynn|title=w:Transfer of Power|genre=fiction|publisher=w:Simon & Schuster|isbn=9781847395757|page=250|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=XvSmFozyMcAC&pg=PT367|passage=Kennedy looked down at Flood's desk and thought about the possibilities. "Can you locate him?"
"I already have my '''people''' checking on all three. So far I've only been able to confirm the whereabouts of the Jordanian officer."}} # {{senseid|en|one's ancestors, relatives, or family}} A person's [[ancestor]]s, [[relative]]s or family. #: {{syn|en|kin|kith|folks}} #: {{ux|en|My '''people''' lived through the Black Plague and the Thirty Years War.}} #: {{ux|en|His '''people''' live out west.}} # {{senseid|en|populace, commonalty}} The mass of a community as distinguished from a special [[class]] (elite); the [[commonalty]]; the [[populace]]; the [[vulgar]]; the common crowd; the [[citizen]]s. #: {{syn|en|populace|commoners|citizenry}} #: {{ux|en|The '''people''' have successfully stood up against tyranny and totalitarianism.}} #: {{ux|en|The election is over and the '''people''' have spoken.}} #: {{ux|en|The '''people''' won't tolerate so much corruption any more!}} # {{senseid|en|humans, humankind}} People in general, humans, by extension sentient beings real or fictional. #: {{ux|en| '''People''' don't like it when you tweak their noses.}} #: {{ux|en|Teachers are '''people''' too.}} =====Usage notes===== * The word ''people'' today takes a plural verb in most senses. * Nowadays, ''persons'' as the plural of ''person'' is considered highly formal. Several major style guides recommend ''people'' rather than ''persons''. For example, the Associated Press and the New York Times recommend ''people'' except in quotations and set phrases. Under the traditional distinction, which {{w|Garner's Modern English Usage|Garner}} says is pedantic,{{R:Garner's|edition=4th|page=682|entry=people}} ''persons'' describes a finite, known number of individuals, rather than the collective term ''people''.
